title: One Phosphate Flips a Waiting Factor

scenes.tts: Add a growth factor to a resting cell, and within minutes it is transcribing a gene called C fos. Now use a drug to stop every ribosome in the cell. The gene still switches on. So whatever switched it on was already made, and waiting. What was waiting there, and what did the signal do to it?
scenes.visual: The cell: membrane on top, a large nucleus below with DNA and the c-fos gene. A growth factor lands, a clock sweeps and the gene turns green. Reset: a drug blocks a ribosomes chip, the factor lands again and the gene still turns green. A dashed question-mark box appears on the DNA in front of the gene, and a dashed arrow of doubt runs to it from the signal.

scenes.tts: A transcription factor is a protein that binds a short DNA sequence near a gene. Making more of a factor is slow, so fast gene responses usually change one already made. One such factor is Creb. It sits in front of C fos as a pair, largely there before any signal arrives. Yet being on the DNA is not enough to switch the gene on.
scenes.visual: The question-mark box becomes a transcription factor chip that lowers onto a short stretch of DNA. A dashed chip for making more factor is struck out beside a slow clock, and the factor on the DNA is labelled already made. It becomes CREB, drawn as a pair, in front of the c-fos gene. The gene stays grey with a crossed-out transcription arrow.

scenes.tts: When C A M P rises, it frees the catalytic subunits of a kinase called P K A. Some of them enter the nucleus. There P K A puts a phosphate on one serine of Creb, serine one thirty-three. That phosphate is a handle, something another protein can hold.
scenes.visual: A cAMP chip meets a PKA blob in the cytoplasm and two small pieces pop free. One piece crosses into the nucleus and becomes a PKA chip, walks to the CREB stalk and passes a gold phosphate onto the serine at its tip. The stalk with its phosphate is labelled a handle.
scenes.caption: When cAMP rises, it frees the catalytic subunits of a kinase called PKA. Some of them enter the nucleus. There PKA puts a phosphate on one serine of CREB, serine 133. That phosphate is a handle, something another protein can hold.

scenes.tts: A co-activator is a helper protein that does not bind DNA itself. The co-activator C B P has a small domain called Kix. Kix grips Creb far more tightly when the phosphate is on. Held at the gene, C B P adds acetyl groups to the histones that package DNA, which loosens them. It also contacts the machinery that brings in R N A polymerase.
scenes.visual: A co-activator blob hovers above the DNA with its DNA grip crossed out, and is named CBP. A pink KIX cup on it closes on the phosphate handle. Acetyl badges fly to a row of histone beads, which loosen. CBP touches a machinery chip, an RNA polymerase chip lands on the gene and the gene turns green.

scenes.tts: Now take a different messenger, calcium. Calcium and calmodulin, helped by an upstream kinase, switch on C a M K four. This kinase is found largely in the nucleus, and it phosphorylates Creb on the same serine. So Creb is a place where messengers meet, and either one adds the same handle. Growth factors reach that serine too, through kinases that E R K switches on.
scenes.visual: A clean nucleus with a bare CREB, and the cAMP route to its serine dimmed on the left. A calcium chip joins calmodulin, switches on CaMKIV in the nucleus, and a phosphate drops onto the same serine. Both kinases point at it. A growth factor route through ERK and kinases arrives at the same serine from the right.

scenes.tts: Now go back to the gene, C fos. Its control region carries a site for Creb. C A M P, calcium and growth factors can each reach the gene through factors already in place. That is why the ribosomes did not matter. So keep this rule: the factor is already made, and the signal changes what it does.
scenes.visual: The opening picture returns: growth factor on the membrane, the ribosomes chip struck out by the drug, and CREB already on its site in front of c-fos. Three signal routes run to CREB, its phosphate handle appears, the gene turns green with the ribosomes still blocked, and the CREB label reads already made, flipped by the signal.
